title: Groupoid laws for prescribed scheme morphisms
statement: Let $U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] be morphisms. These data form an (absolute) groupoid scheme if, for every test scheme $H$, the sets $U(H)=\operatorname{Hom}(H,U)$ and $R(H)=\operatorname{Hom}(H,R)$ are respectively objects and arrows of a groupoid, with the operations induced by $s,t,e,i,c$, naturally under precomposition in $H$. Explicitly, $se=te=\mathrm{id}_U$, $si=t$, $ti=s$, $sc=s\operatorname{pr}_1$, $tc=t\operatorname{pr}_0$, and on $H$-points $c(e(t(a)),a)=a$, $c(a,e(s(a)))=a$, $c(i(a),a)=e(s(a))$, $c(a,i(a))=e(t(a))$ and $c(c(a,b),d)=c(a,c(b,d))$ whenever $s(a)=t(b)$ and $s(b)=t(d)$. Here $c(a,b)$ means composition with the unique map into the fibre product having projections $a,b$.
